questions.knowledgeNote: From x - y = 2 read x = 2+y and substitute, or eliminate directly; both give the same single step.
questions.question: Q1(b). Solve by both addition method and row-equivalent matrices: x - y = 2; 2x + 3y = 9.
questions.solution: Addition: 2×(first)-(second): 2x-2y-2x-3y = 4-9, so -5y = -5, y = 1; then x = 2+1 = 3. Row-equivalent: [1 -1 : 2; 2 3 : 9] → R2→R2-2R1 = [1 -1 : 2; 0 5 : 5] → R2→R2/5 → R1→R1+R2 gives [1 0 : 3; 0 1 : 1]. Boxed (3,1). Verify: 3-1 = 2 ✓; 6+3 = 9 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q1(b); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Kill x first from two pairs, leaving a 2×2 in y,z; solve it, then back-substitute up the chain.
questions.question: Q1(c). Solve by both addition method and row-equivalent matrices: x + y - 2z = 7; 2x - 3y - 2z = 0; x - 2y - 3z = 3.
questions.solution: Addition: 2×(first)-(second): 5y-2z = 14. (first)-(third): 3y+z = 4, so z = 4-3y; then 5y-2(4-3y) = 14 gives 11y = 22, y = 2, z = -2, x = 7-2-4 = 1. Row-equivalent: reduce [1 1 -2 : 7; 2 -3 -2 : 0; 1 -2 -3 : 3] by R2→R2-2R1, R3→R3-R1, then R3→R3-(3/5)R2, scale and back-eliminate to [I : 1; 2; -2]. Boxed (1,2,-2). Verify in second: 2-6+4 = 0 ✓; third: 1-4+6 = 3 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q1(c); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(c). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: x + y + z = 1; x + 2y + 3z = 4; x + 3y + 7z = 13. (T.U. 2051)
questions.solution: R2→R2-R1: y+2z = 3. R3→R3-R1: 2y+6z = 12, i.e. y+3z = 6. Subtracting: z = 3; then y = 3-6 = -3; x = 1-(-3)-3 = 1. Row-equivalent: same steps on [1 1 1 : 1; 1 2 3 : 4; 1 3 7 : 13] reach [I : 1; -3; 3]. Boxed (1,-3,3). Verify in third: 1-9+21 = 13 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q3(c) (T.U. 2051); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read; answer p299 = PDF p326)

questions.question: Q3(e). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: 9y - 5x = 3; x + z = 1; z + 2y = 2.
questions.solution: From x+z = 1, x = 1-z; from z+2y = 2, z = 2-2y, so x = 2y-1. In -5x+9y = 3: -5(2y-1)+9y = 3 gives -y+5 = 3, y = 2; then z = -2, x = 3. Row ops on [-5 9 0 : 3; 1 0 1 : 1; 0 2 1 : 2] reach [I : 3; 2; -2]. Boxed (3,2,-2). Verify: 18-15 = 3 ✓; 3-2 = 1 ✓; -2+4 = 2 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q3(e); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read; answer p299 = PDF p326)

questions.knowledgeNote: Row 2 has z = 0, so 3x+9y = 18 gives x = 6-3y first; feed it into the other two.
questions.question: Q3(f). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: x + 4y + 3z = 6; 3x + 9y = 18; -5x - 6y + 2z = -5.
questions.solution: From row 2: x+3y = 6, x = 6-3y. Row 1: 6-3y+4y+3z = 6, so y+3z = 0, y = -3z. Row 3: -5(6-3y)-6y+2z = -5 gives -30+9y+2z = -5, 9y+2z = 25; with y = -3z: -27z+2z = 25, z = -1, y = 3, x = -3. Boxed (-3,3,-1). Verify in row 1: -3+12-3 = 6 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q3(f); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read; answer p299 = PDF p326)

questions.knowledgeNote: Adding the first two rows kills y and z at once: 2x = 4.
questions.question: Q3(g). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: x - y + z = -3; x + y + z = 1; 3x - 4y - z = 1.
questions.solution: Adding first+second gives 2x+2z = -2, i.e. x+z = -1. Subtracting first from second: 2y = 4, y = 2. Then x+z = -1 and 3x-z = 1+4y = 9, so 3x-z = 9; with z = -1-x: 3x+1+x = 9, 4x = 8, x = 2, z = -3. Boxed (2,2,-3). Verify in third: 6-8+3 = 1 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q3(g); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read; answer p299 = PDF p326)

questions.question: Q3(i). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: 2y + 6z = 2; 3y + 6z = 6; 2x + 4y + 6z = 22.
questions.solution: (second)-(first): y = 4. Then 8+6z = 2, z = -1. Third: 2x+16-6 = 22, 2x = 12, x = 6. Boxed (6,4,-1). Verify in third: 12+16-6 = 22 ✓ (matches the printed key).

questions.knowledgeNote: Row 3 gives z = 4y-7; eliminate z from the first two, then solve the 2×2 in x,y.
questions.question: Q3(j). Use row-equivalent matrices to solve: x + 4y + z = 18; 3x + 3y - 2z = 2; -4y + z = -7.
questions.solution: z = 4y-7. Row 1: x+4y+4y-7 = 18, x+8y = 25. Row 2: 3x+3y-2(4y-7) = 2, 3x-5y = -12. From first: x = 25-8y; then 3(25-8y)-5y = -12 gives 75-29y = -12, y = 3; x = 1; z = 5. Boxed (1,3,5). Verify in row 2: 3+9-10 = 2 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.2 Q3(j); book p298 = PDF p325 (vision read; answer p299 = PDF p326)
